idea-plugin.name: Git-Aware Dev Journal
idea-plugin.description:
Git-Aware Dev Journal — Remember Why You Wrote That Code

A development journal that links notes to your git context. Every entry captures the commit, branch, and file position automatically. Stop losing the reasoning behind your code decisions.

Features

  • Git-Linked Notes — Entries auto-linked to commit hash, branch, and file position
  • 6 Entry Types — Notes, Decisions, TODOs, Blockers, Insights, Questions
  • Auto-Capture — Conventional commits parsed into journal entries automatically
  • Branch Narratives — Auto-generated story of your work on each branch
  • Timeline View — Chronological view with search and filters
  • Code Hover Context — See why code was written by hovering over annotated lines
  • Standup generator (Markdown/Slack format)
  • PR/MR summary generator
  • Unlimited notes
  • Cross-device sync
  • Team sharing via .dev-journal/ directory
  • Export (Markdown, JSON, CSV)

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1+ (or any JetBrains IDE)
  • Git repository

Support

Documentation | Issue Tracker | Contact Support

action.description: Add a development journal entry at the current cursor position

idea-plugin.change-notes:
What's New

  • Git-Linked Journal Entries - Notes automatically linked to commit hash, branch, and file position
  • Six Entry Types - Notes, Decisions, TODOs, Blockers, Insights, and Questions for organized journaling
  • Auto-Capture from Commits - Conventional commits (feat, fix, docs, refactor) are automatically parsed into journal entries
  • Branch Narratives - Auto-generated story of your work on each branch
  • Timeline View - Chronological view of all entries with filtering and search
  • Code Hover Context - See why code was written by hovering over annotated lines
  • Blame View Integration - Extra note column in git blame showing associated journal entries
  • Standup Generator - Generate Markdown or Slack-compatible standup reports from your journal
  • PR Summary Generator - Create pull request descriptions from journal entries
  • Team Sharing - Share journal entries via .dev-journal/ directory in your repository
